description: Three managers: the Python package (pyproject.toml and uv.lock), the UI (ui/package.json and its lockfile), and the GitHub Actions. uv.lock picks each release CI and the golden tests run, so every bump arrives as a pull request those tests gate. The MCP bundle's pyproject.toml is left out: the release sets its pins.

lockFileMaintenance.description: On, weekly, for uv.lock: uv holds a refresh to the 14-day wait (exclude-newer in pyproject.toml), exempting only NimbleBrain's own packages. A refresh that moves nimblebrain-server-sdk fails tests/test_mcpb.py until mcpb/pyproject.toml's constraint moves with it in the same pull request. npm cannot hold a refresh to the wait, so ui's lockfile changes only with a dependency bump.

packageRules.description: The MCP bundle pins the released package and holds the SDK to the version in uv.lock (tests/test_mcpb.py); the release moves both, never Renovate.

Golden tests hold the wire contracts nimblebrain-server-sdk and pgkeyset produce. pgkeyset is pinned exactly; the SDK is held to a minor range and uv.lock picks its version. A bump of either is a deliberate, reviewed change, never part of a group.
